senses.gloss: f. (preced. wds.) love, esteem, honor. Koh. K. to V, 14 בא לעולם בח׳ וכ׳ man enters the world with love (caressed by his nearest), and leaves with love.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bikkurim 2:1:8">Y. Bicc. II, 64ᵈ</cite> top <he>לשבעה מיתה של ח׳</he> a death after seven days of sickness is a death of (divine) love; (ib.ᶜ bot. <he>לשבעים מיתה של ח׳</he>, read <cite ref="U00788"><he>שֵׂיבָה</he></cite>).—
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 3:14">Ab. III, 14</cite> <he>ח׳ יתירה וכ׳</he> the greater divine love consists in its being made known to him &c.

<cite ref="Chullin 33a">Ḥull. 33ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>חִיבַּת הקדש מכשרתן</he> the honor in which sacred objects are held makes them fit for levitical uncleanness (even without contact with liquids, v. <cite ref="K01327"><he>כָּשַׁר</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 2:6">Ex. R. s. 2</cite>, a. fr. <he>לשון ח׳</he> the repetition of a name intimates endearment.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 4:6:5">Y. Succ. IV, 54ᵈ</cite> top <he>לשון ח׳</he> (the word <cite ref="U01187"><he>שֵׁכָר</he></cite>, <cite ref="Numbers 28:7">Num. XXVIII, 7</cite>) expresses something dear; (Bab. ib. 49ᵇ; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 21">Num. R. s. 21</cite> <cite ref="U02102"><he>שתייה</he></cite>).—
<cite ref="Ketubot 56a:6">Keth. 56ᵃ</cite> <he>חיבת חופה וכ׳</he> the affection produced by the seclusion in the bridal department is the final act of possession.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 93">Gen. R. s. 93</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 150">Yalk. ib. 150</cite> [read:] <he>על חיבת העין כך על בעל אכסניא וכ׳</he> if this was done for a dear object of sight (our sister), how much more shall we do in defence of the host of the Lord (Benjamin, v. <cite ref="A00934"><he>אוּשְׁפִּיזְכָן</he></cite>); a. fr.—Ch. <cite ref="H00660"><he>חִיבְּתָא</he></cite>.
